papers.title: Origin of long-lived nuclear spin states and coherences in aliphatic chains revealed by relaxation theory
papers.authors: Danil A. Markelov, Kirill F. Sheberstov
papers.summary: Relaxation theory constructs long-lived nuclear-spin states and coherences in aliphatic chains from protected modes of the dipolar relaxation operator. Simulations reproduce observed decay dynamics and clarify which collective modes are experimentally accessible.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful molecular-spin example of protection emerging from symmetry and correlated relaxation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate routes to long-lived molecular quantum states, with different spin species.

papers.title: Quantifying the Spin–Optical Properties of Bent π-Carbene Molecular Qubits
papers.authors: Yong Rui Poh, Xiao Chen, Hai-Ping Cheng, Joel Yuen-Zhou
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.summary: A minimal Hamiltonian describes competing spin-selective intersystem-crossing channels in bent π-carbene qubits. Analytical results and electronic-structure calculations suggest design choices that suppress unwanted pathways while preserving optical spin preparation.
papers.whyRelevant: A direct molecular-design reference for balancing spin polarization, optical transitions and open-shell structure.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect molecular electronic structure with optical properties of radical-based qubits.

papers.title: High-Spin-Locked Fe(II) Spin-Crossover Compounds: THz-EPR Investigations and Spin–Phonon Coupling
papers.authors: Tarek Al Said, Eike Kuhlemann, Haowei Chen, Maurice van Gastel, Marcel Walter, Malte Laurin Schwank, Sangeeta Thakur, Karsten Holldack, Wolfgang Kuch, Felix Tuczek, Frank Neese
papers.summary: THz-EPR measurements probe low-temperature high-spin states in two iron spin-crossover compounds. Modeling resolves zero-field splitting and requires explicit spin–phonon coupling to account for one compound's field-dependent transitions.
papers.whyRelevant: A spectroscopic case study for recognizing when a spin-only Hamiltonian is insufficient.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate experimentally consequential spin–phonon coupling.

papers.title: High-fidelity molecular quantum logic gates resilient to interaction fluctuation
papers.summary: A theoretical molecular controlled-phase gate combines global microwave pulses with spin-echo-like protection. Modeling of trapped-molecule motion indicates reduced sensitivity to fluctuating dipole interactions and a tunable controlled phase.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to robust molecular quantum control, with performance estimates that remain theoretical.

relatedPapers.reason: Both seek to reduce errors through the structure of control sequences.

papers.title: Very high frequency (263 GHz) pulse EPR spectroscopy of high spin transition metal centers
papers.authors: Zikri Hasanbasri, Shasha Qiu, Guodong Rao, Amanda Caceres, Erica Debley, Yuan Zheng, Elizabeth M. Nolan, Marie Heffern, Paul Stucky, Neville C. Luhmann Jr, R. David Britt
papers.summary: A high-power millimeter-wave amplifier extends pulsed EPR operation to 263 GHz. Measurements on high-spin manganese centers illustrate how the instrument accesses broad transitions and produces spin echoes without a resonator.
papers.whyRelevant: A concrete instrumentation reference for high-field studies of molecular ions and zero-field-splitting effects.

relatedPapers.reason: Both depend on experimentally addressing molecular electron-spin transitions.

papers.title: Ultrafast spin-transfer dynamics and single-qubit logic gate design in monocyclic carbon rings with transition metal atoms adsorbed
papers.authors: Yan Wu, Shangjie Ma, Ronghua Chen, Shuai Xu, Yiming Zhang, Jing Liu, Chun Li, Georgios Lefkidis, Wolfgang Hübner, Wei Jin
papers.summary: First-principles simulations examine laser-driven spin transfer in transition-metal-decorated carbon rings. Tailored pulses implement proposed single-qubit gates, with detuning and chirp tests probing their tolerance to control variations.
papers.whyRelevant: A molecular spin-control design study that should be read as a theoretical proposal rather than a demonstrated processor.

relatedPapers.reason: Both target coherent manipulation of localized molecular electron spins.

papers.title: Quantitative Quantum Relaxometry Framework for Probing Transient Radical-Associated Magnetic Fluctuations under Operando Conditions
papers.authors: Zenghao Kong, Jia Su, Jiasong Li, Fazhan Shi
papers.summary: NV relaxometry links transient radical-associated magnetic noise to changes in longitudinal relaxation. The work develops a quantitative framework and demonstrates operando tracking during photocatalytic water splitting.
papers.whyRelevant: A strong methods reference for connecting radical dynamics, magnetic fluctuations and a measurable sensing signal.

relatedPapers.reason: Both infer environmental dynamics from molecular or defect spin relaxation.

papers.title: Electrical Readout of Spin Environments in Diamond for Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Olga Rubinas, Michael Petrov, Emilie Bourgeois, Jaroslav Hruby, Akhil Kuriakose, Ottavia Jedrkiewicz, Milos Nesladek
papers.summary: Photocurrent-detected DEER reads interactions between diamond NV centers and nearby paramagnetic defects. The experiment identifies nitrogen-related spin-bath species using electrical detection instead of conventional fluorescence collection.
papers.whyRelevant: A concrete route for combining spin-environment characterization with compact electrical readout.

relatedPapers.reason: Both infer a local environment from its influence on a spin probe.

papers.title: Multiparametric quantum sensing of liquids using NV centers and tethered magnetic nanoparticles
papers.authors: Johannes Fiedler, Martin Møller Greve, Justas Zalieckas
papers.summary: A proposed liquid-sensing platform couples near-surface NV centers to magnetic nanoparticles tethered by DNA. Spatially varied tethers would translate liquid-dependent motion into multiple magnetic response channels.
papers.whyRelevant: A conceptual comparison for viscosity-sensitive spin probes; the paper outlines a proposal rather than validating a complete device.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use environment-dependent dynamics to probe properties of liquids.

papers.title: Engineering Intrinsic Mixed Sodium Ionic–Electronic Conductivity in a Nickel Bis(diimine) Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Xinyi Zhou, Dongxu Chen, Jinxin Liu, Mingyu Yang, Yuting Zeng, Shiyan Xiao, Zheng Meng
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Sulfonate side chains introduce sodium-ion pathways into a conductive nickel bis(diimine) MOF. Electrical measurements resolve intrinsic ionic and electronic transport, while structural analysis links each contribution to a different part of the framework.
papers.whyRelevant: Especially relevant when distinguishing ionic motion from electronic conductivity in functionalized conductive MOFs.

relatedPapers.reason: Both highlight the need to separate mechanisms behind measured framework conductivity.

papers.title: Termination-Controlled Fractional Spin Modes at Organic Topological Spin–Chain Interfaces
papers.summary: A theoretical organic radical-chain study compares terminations at interfaces between different spin sectors. Changing the bond registry can quench or retain localized fractional spin modes and tune their coupling across a finite domain.
papers.whyRelevant: Connects atomically defined molecular interfaces to emergent local spin behavior.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern extended organic radical architectures and their spin properties.

papers.title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Based Optoelectronic Memristors: Structural Design, Optoelectronic Modulation and Neuromorphic Applications
papers.authors: Xianglong Dai, Qiongshan Zhang, Bin Zhang
papers.summary: This review maps COF chemistry and stacking onto light-controlled conductance and memory effects. It distinguishes proposed mechanisms and simulated functions from experimentally resolved device states, emphasizing contacts, film quality and reversibility.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful framework for evaluating whether an observed conductance change has a demonstrated microscopic mechanism.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect framework structure and film or crystal quality with device behavior.

papers.title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
papers.authors: Xingxing Zhong, Mian Wei, Jing-Kai Wang, Yuqing Zhang, Xiaoyan Jiang, Jianhua Yu, Xiang Zhao
papers.summary: Lower-symmetry linkers distort a MOF network so that only part of its pore space is partitioned. The resulting architecture retains accessible metal sites and changes gas-separation selectivity relative to fully partitioned analogues.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides a concrete strategy for controlling local coordination environments through linker symmetry.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use synthetic control to engineer well-defined framework structures.

papers.title: Solvent‐Free Synthesis of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Achievements and Challenges
papers.authors: Qingyun Zhang, Kaiyuan Wang, Dong Wang, Meiting Zhao, Zhenjie Zhang, Zhifang Wang
papers.summary: This minireview compares mechanochemical, ionothermal, melt-assisted and vapor-assisted COF synthesis. It examines how alternative reaction environments affect crystallization, shaping and reproducible scale-up.
papers.whyRelevant: A compact synthesis map for evaluating alternatives to conventional solvothermal crystal growth.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address the balance between reaction pathways and crystallization.

papers.title: Intrinsic Near‐Infrared Photothermal Effect Induces Single‐Crystal‐to‐Single‐Crystal Transformation in Organic Molecular Crystals
papers.authors: Liming Yang, Binjie Chen, Rushuai Deng, Xiangwei Kong, Yunze Huang, Mingxing Chen, Xinggui Gu
papers.summary: Near-infrared photothermal excitation drives a single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformation in an organic crystal. Structural measurements and calculations connect conformational flexibility with retained lattice order and controlled guest release.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a crystal-engineering example of changing local structure while preserving long-range order.

relatedPapers.reason: Both depend on controlling structural order in molecular crystalline materials.

selectionPolicy: Historical reconstruction by publication date, not discovery date: prefer papers published in the issue date or previous six days; only if fewer than three qualify in a direction, supplement from publication ages 7–29 days to reach three. Maximum five per direction; exclude existing library records and every other issue. First discovery and preparation timestamps retain their actual dates.
